title: Five-Hole Generalization Benchmark: Pandey-Kumar (2025) Section 4.4 Figures 22-25 Reproduction, Arbitrary Multi-Hole Geometry Extension, and Constitutive Split Assessment
objectives: Stage 1: Extract exact five-hole benchmark parameters from Pandey & Kumar (2025) Section 4.4 (geometry, hole coordinates, boundary conditions, material properties, fracture length scale, and Amor volumetric-deviatoric constitutive split).

Stage 2: Assess constitutive UEL formulation compatibility (Amor volumetric-deviatoric split vs spectral Miehe split) and determine whether canonical UEL can be qualified directly or requires a separately versioned UEL variant.
Stage 3: Extend reusable geometry adapter and meshing infrastructure to support arbitrary lists of holes, smooth boundaries without initial notches, and multiple independent nucleation zones.

Stage 4: Generate authentic five-hole geometry and coarse FE mesh; execute Abaqus linear elastic pre-analysis solve and extract genuine Superconvergent Patch Recovery (SPR) MISESERI error indicator field.
Stage 5: Generate new adapted physical mesh using indicator-driven sizing without any hardcoded crack paths or geometric proxies; audit Jacobians, element quality, and spatial resolution.
Stage 6: Build multi-layer production deck, perform local and cluster datachecks, route independent review via PAD bridge, and prepare governed PBS execution manifest under once-only accounting.
